newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bourse clears way for listing of MTNs.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bourse clears way for listing of MTNs.

text.p: The Swiss Stock exchange has agreed to allow Swiss franc tranches of medium-term note (MTN) programmes to be listed in Switzerland, stock exchange officials and market sources said.

After roughly a year of talks between lead managers and the Stock Exchange Admissions Board, which is the body at the Swiss stock exchange which deals with listings, the first such listings were approved last week, according to lead managers.
The listings approved so far have pertained to European Medium Term Note programmes set up under English law.
A bourse official said that in future, listings for MTNs issued under U.S. law were also likely to be allowed.
"Talks are open to MTNs under American law. The first ones we have are under English law. We expect others to follow," the bourse official said, who declined to be quoted by name.
A MTN is a loan programme which enables the borrower to issue notes in several currencies. The notes are issued under a framework legal agreement.
Such a programme saves borrowers the time, trouble and expense of seeking separate facilities for every bond issued.
Until the Swiss Stock Exchange granted its approval, Swiss franc MTNs were not allowed to be listed on Switzerland's stock exchange. They could be launched only as private placements.

The approval so far has allowed at least four Swiss franc issues for foreign borrowers to be listed. The decision effectively means that foreign law is applied with respect to payment obligations and legal regulations governing issuance.
The listings approved thus far comprise offerings led by Credit Suisse or Merrill Lynch. Both firms said they have been in extensive talks with the exchange.
The Credit Suisse-led offerings comprise a floating rate bond for a unit of Spanish utility Endesa, an offering for Transpower New Zealand, and an issue for Energie Beheer Nederland.

Approval was also granted for a Swiss franc issue for a unit of Anglo-American pharmaceuticals firm Smithkline Beecham, led by Merrill. Approval is pending for another offering for Smithkline Beecham, a 125 million Swiss franc issue launched last Thursday and also led by Merrill.
Paul Dennison, managing director at Merrill Lynch Capital Markets Ltd in Zurich said the Swiss stock exchange's approval should pave the way for further similar deals.
"Now that the deal is listed, we and others will bring more deals listed on the stock exchange," Dennison said.
Hans Keller, a member of senior managment at Credit Suisse, also expected more such issues after the bourse ruling.
"We have a new model, and further issues of this sort are certainly to be expected," Keller said.
Sources said that the Swiss stock exchange would still require that Swiss laws apply with respect to protection for retail investors.
"They are keen to know that the private investor particularly ... has the right to sue ... to protect his interest as they understand it under Swiss law," one source said.
